name: pricing-calculator
title: Pricing: Usage calculator
description: Usage pricing with a slider for invoices a month: the price, the plan it falls in and the cost per invoice follow as you drag.

files.content:
"use client" // Pricing, usage calculator: graduated pricing per invoice, worked out live from a slider. The price, the // plan the volume falls in and the cost per invoice follow the slider, and the rate card shows how the // total is made up. A polite live region reads the result once the slider settles, not on every step. import { ArrowRight } from "lucide-react" import { useEffect, useId, useState } from "react" import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button" import { Slider } from "@/components/ui/slider" import { cn } from "@/lib/utils" const MAX = 1000 const TIERS = [ { plan: "Free", from: 0, to: 10, rate: 0, range: "First 10 invoices" }, { plan: "Studio", from: 10, to: 100, rate: 0.5, range: "11 to 100" }, { plan: "Agency", from: 100, to: 500, rate: 0.3, range: "101 to 500" }, { plan: "Scale", from: 500, to: Infinity, rate: 0.2, range: "501 and up" }, ] const money = (n: number) => new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD", minimumFractionDigits: Number.isInteger(n) ? 0 : 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 }).format(n) const count = (n: number) => new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US").format(n) function quote(n: number) { const lines = TIERS.map((t) => { const used = Math.max(0, Math.min(n, t.to) - t.from) return { ...t, used, subtotal: used * t.rate } }) const total = lines.reduce((s, l) => s + l.subtotal, 0) const tier = TIERS.find((t) => n <= t.to) ?? TIERS[TIERS.length - 1] return { lines, total, plan: tier.plan, each: n ? total / n : 0 } } export default function PricingCalculator() { const id = useId() const [invoices, setInvoices] = useState(120) const q = quote(invoices) const summary = `${count(invoices)} invoices a month: ${money(q.total)} a month on the ${q.plan} plan${q.total ? `, ${money(q.each)} an invoice` : ""}.` // Announce once the value has been still for a moment, so dragging doesn't read out every step. const [announced, setAnnounced] = useState("") useEffect(() => { const t = setTimeout(() => setAnnounced(summary), 700) return () => clearTimeout(t) }, [summary]) return (
